title: Class delegation with by
context: What does class delegation with `by` do, and how does it differ from inheritance?

refs.title: Atomic Kotlin (book) by Bruce Eckel & Svetlana Isakova

answer: `class Repo(store: Store) : Store by store` implements every Store method by forwarding to the store object. You can then override only the methods you want to change. Delegation favours composition: the wrapper has a Store rather than being one, so you avoid fragile base-class problems. It needs an interface to delegate. Use it to add behaviour, such as logging or caching, around an existing implementation.

points.title: Forwarding
points.why: Methods of the interface are forwarded to the delegate object automatically.

points.title: Composition over inheritance
points.why: The wrapper depends on an interface, not on a base class's internals.
